$description: Green Control design tokens, W3C Design Tokens (DTCG) format. Two themes share one set of names: night (default) and day. Three layers since v1.5: primitive (raw colours) → semantic (what a colour means) → component (which part uses it). Themes only re-point semantic tokens; components never change.

color.$description: Raw colours. Never used directly in UI code: always go through a semantic token in color.*.

graphite-950.$description: Night page, and dark text on light fills (merged with #121214 in v1.5: the two were indistinguishable, ΔE 0.4).

graphite-400.$description: Night secondary text. v1.5: lightened from #8c9199 to pass 4.5:1 on raised backgrounds.

paper-600.$description: Day secondary text. v1.5: darkened from #6e6e69 to pass 4.5:1 on raised and chip backgrounds.

bg-surface.$description: Panels and cards that sit on the page.

bg-raised.$description: Blocks inside a surface: rows, chips, user messages.

text.$description: Primary text. Also the primary button at night.

muted.$description: Secondary text, finished steps, idle icons.

accent.$description: The one signal colour. Night: the problem and the step in progress. Day: also links and selection. Never decorative.

link.$description: Object links (machines, teams, work orders). Night: text colour. Day: accent.

cta-bg.$description: Primary button fill. One per view.

color.$description: Semantic and component colours. Each value points at a primitive. Day values live in $extensions.day. layer = semantic (what it means) or component (which part uses it).

glass.$description: Frosted panels that float over the drawing. Always with blur 24px.

sheen.$description: Top-down sheen on glass and blocks.

edge-hi.$description: 1px inner top highlight on glass and blocks.

dot.$description: Dot field behind the drawing: 0.55px dots on a 4.2px pitch, masked so it fades before guides.

pool.$description: Soft radial glow under the object in focus.

none.$description: Every surface, button and chip is square.

dot.$description: Only for status dots and spinners.

mono.$description: Labels, data, timestamps. Never for sentences.

motion.$description: Chosen by what a movement does, not by component. No other durations or curves; a long one-off sequence (the figure assembling, the scan) is written inside its component and marked as an exception.

ease.$description: Fast start, soft stop. Everything that enters or moves.

exit.$description: Slow start, fast finish. Everything that leaves, so it doesn't linger at the end.

spring.$description: Overshoots a little. Only for things that arrive: toasts, badges, a landed check.

wave.$description: Back and forth. Only for loops that mean 'still going'.

linear.$description: Constant speed. Only for things that spin or flow: a spinner, a progress sheen.

feedback.$description: Hover and press. Past about 0.1 s a hand feels the screen didn't answer.

small-out.$description: A label, chip or popover leaving. Leaving is one step shorter than arriving.

small-in.$description: A label, chip or popover arriving. Short distance, short time.

in.$description: A panel or sheet arriving, or a new line landing in the thread. Long enough to see where it came from.

rise.$description: Old name for `in`, kept so existing code works.

move.$description: Layout changes: the rail folding, overview to equipment. The whole page moves, so the eye needs time to follow.

camera.$description: The drawing turning or zooming. The biggest thing on screen, so the slowest.

loop.$description: One cycle of something in progress: the AI thinking, a spinner, a scan ring.

ambient.$description: One cycle of something live: the live dot, a pulse on a hot spot. Slow, so it never pulls the eye from a fault.

confidence-act.$description: At or above: the AI may propose a plan with an Apply button.

confidence-review.$description: 50 to 79: the plan is shown as a draft; evidence opens by default; the person reviews before applying.

undo-window.$description: Every action the AI applies can be undone from the toast or the Actions timeline.
